before:
Pump Attendance — Order of Call

The board keeps one attendant on night cover for the three installations on the lower drain. Nothing here alters what the attendant may or may not do at any installation; the standing instructions for each remain in force, including logging arrival and departure at the cabin telephone. Where two or more installations call within the same half hour, the attendant answers the sluice station first, then the washland pump, and the roadside gully last. Travelling time between the three is roughly twenty minutes in either direction, and the attendant should telephone the duty clerk before leaving any site unattended for longer than that. Fuel returns are collected at the end of the shift as usual.

before:
Ringers' Register — Tower Key

The register is kept in the vestry cupboard and shows, for each member, the date of joining, the last handling assessment, and any period of suspension. Members who have completed the handling assessment may take the tower key from the vestry box at any reasonable hour without further authority, provided they enter the time of removal and return on the facing page. Members who have not yet been assessed may enter the ringing chamber only in company with an assessed member. The steeple keeper reviews the facing page each quarter and reports omissions to the churchwardens, who keep the spare key in the parish safe.
after:
Ringers' Register — Tower Key

The register is kept in the vestry cupboard and shows, for each member, the date of joining, the last handling assessment, and any period of suspension. Members who have completed the handling assessment must obtain the steeple keeper's consent on each occasion before taking the tower key from the vestry box, provided they enter the time of removal and return on the facing page. Members who have not yet been assessed may enter the ringing chamber only in company with an assessed member. The steeple keeper reviews the facing page each quarter and reports omissions to the churchwardens, who keep the spare key in the parish safe.
variation_site: The passage concerns access to the tower key by assessed members.
author_note: Converts an open permission into a required consent, leaving the register's contents and the facing-page entries untouched.

before:

Present: seven members; apologies from two. The treasurer reported takings of eleven pounds forty from the February drive, which is consistent with attendance of thirty-one. before:
Estuary Bulletin — Silt Bar, Number 3 Reach

Soundings were taken from the launch on two mornings this month at low water springs. The channel between the perches remains navigable at half tide for craft drawing under a metre. On the evidence of a single line of soundings, the bar appears to have moved some forty metres northward since the survey of two winters ago. Skippers using the reach at night are asked to give the eastern perch a wide berth until the next full survey, which the harbour office expects to arrange before the equinox. Copies of the sounding sheets may be consulted at the office counter during weekday mornings.

before:
Handbook — Kiln Firing, Pre-Heat Checks

The same three checks are made by the firer before every biscuit firing, and none of them may be omitted. Working alone at the panel, the firer sets the damper to the quarter mark, then zeroes the pyrometer against the cold junction, then opens the flue observation slide and confirms a clear draught. Each check is initialled in the firing book against the clock time. If any check cannot be completed the firing is not started and the kiln steward is telephoned. Nothing in these paragraphs changes what the firer is obliged to do or what may be fired; the times entered in the book remain the record for insurance.

before:
Report — Reservoir Yield, Upper Catchment

Throughout this report the design drought is taken to be the driest twelve months in the last fifty years of gauged flow. Table 2 gives the yield available under that condition at each of the three drawoff levels; Table 3 converts those yields to days of supply at the current demand; and the sensitivity figures in the appendix are expressed as percentages of the Table 2 values. The compensation flow is held constant throughout at the statutory figure. Readers comparing these numbers with the neighbouring authority's report should note that its gauging period is shorter and its catchment partly afforested.

before:
Gate Controller — Night Settings

The compound gate controller is set from the keypad in the weighbridge hut. Night mode runs from 18:30 to 06:00 and holds the barrier down between those times, with the intercom routed to the duty mobile. Unattended vehicles are permitted to stand inside the compound overnight, and the yardman notes their registration in the gate book at close of shift. The lamp on the mast is on a photocell and is not controlled from the keypad. Any change to the night mode times is made only by the yard manager, who holds the second keypad code and the controller handbook in the site office.
